Richard Nixon. The thirty-seventh President of the United States, serving from nineteen sixty-nine until his resignation in nineteen seventy-four. A Cold War strategist who pursued détente with the Soviet Union and opened diplomatic relations with China, he was also a polarizing figure whose presidency ended in disgrace due to the Watergate scandal. He represents both the summit of Cold War realpolitik and the depth of presidential abuse of power.

Nixon built his career as a staunch anti-Communist. He lost the nineteen sixty presidential election to JFK and the nineteen sixty-two California gubernatorial race, declaring his political death when he said people wouldn't have Nixon to kick around anymore. He returned to politics in nineteen sixty-eight with a law and order message, winning the presidency with a narrow plurality. He promised to end the Vietnam War with honor while pursuing aggressive bombing campaigns. He expanded the war into Cambodia in nineteen seventy, sparking massive protests and the Kent State shooting. The war under Nixon killed tens of thousands and expanded beyond Vietnam without Congressional approval.

Nixon pioneered détente with the Soviet Union, signing the Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty, or SALT One, and reducing Cold War tensions through diplomatic engagement. In nineteen seventy-one, he opened relations with Communist China, a stunning reversal of Cold War orthodoxy that increased United States flexibility in the Cold War triangle. He created the silent majority political narrative, appealing to working-class and middle-class Americans he claimed the liberal establishment ignored, using targeted media and messaging to polarize the nation.

Nixon engaged in systematic abuse of power. He compiled an enemies list and authorized the burglary of the Democratic National Committee headquarters at Watergate in June nineteen seventy-two. He then orchestrated a cover-up that unraveled through nineteen seventy-three to nineteen seventy-four. He resigned in August nineteen seventy-four when impeachment and conviction became certain, becoming the only president to resign from office and replaced by Vice President Gerald Ford.
